used: Artificial scarcity reads as value, and exclusion reads as quality.
Add up the Tuesdays spent in the waiting room.
Continually deferring satisfaction spends the present as a means, never an end.
Offer the crowd a role: believe loudly, and you belong.
Let brilliance excuse the parts that do not add up yet.
Charge attention as rent on a building with no keys.
Discard the old, including the lesson.
Attention spent on anticipation is a finite resource drained without return.
Reward staying on the treadmill with a faster treadmill.
Make the goal so large that no particular failure can touch it.
Borrow against today to furnish a tomorrow that ships late.
The halo effect allows genius in one domain to be quietly spent as credibility in another.
The cost of perpetual anticipation is invisible because it is paid in ordinary, un-itemized hours.
